addresses.name: CBuildingDataBase_RoleByModifierId
addresses.comment: The building-role ladder in the building-database loader. eax = building->+0xC, the CModifier the building's one modifier key mapped to, then five compares of the modifier id at CModifier +0x24: 0x2E MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY -> db +0x1C, 0x2D MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY -> db +0x20, 0x4B MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA -> db +0x24, 0x0F MODIFIER_IC -> db +0x2C, 0x66 MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNDERGROUND -> db +0x28. In vanilla and in BlackICE that is air_base, naval_base, anti_air, industry and underground. It is an if/else ladder with no break, so where two buildings carry the same modifier the last one parsed takes the slot. The defaults are set at rva 0xB769B, which points all five slots at the built-in 'nobuilding'.
addresses.evidence: The four CProvince fields are set in one place, the province reset at rva 0x96480, and each is province->buildings[g_CBuildingDataBase->slot->CBuilding::index], with buildings the array already recorded at CProvince +0x310 and index the field already recorded at CBuilding +0x54: rva 0x9694F stores from slot +0x1C into +0x304, rva 0x969D7 from +0x20 into +0x300, rva 0x968C7 from +0x24 into +0x308 and rva 0x96A5F from +0x28 into +0x30C. Which building sits in which database slot is settled by the building-database loader at rva 0xB75E0, called once from rva 0x237067: at rva 0xB769B it points all five role slots (+0x1C, +0x20, +0x24, +0x28, +0x2C) at the built-in 'nobuilding' placeholder, which rva 0xB7510 constructs from the literal at 0x15C09A8, and then, for every building it parses, runs the ladder at rvas 0xB78AB..0xB78F2: eax = building->+0xC, the CModifier its one modifier key mapped to, then five compares of eax->+0x24 against 0x2E -> +0x1C, 0x2D -> +0x20, 0x4B -> +0x24, 0x0F -> +0x2C and 0x66 -> +0x28. Those constants are CModifier ids. The id reaches a CModifier in EDX: its constructor at rva 0x56D50 does mov [esi+0x24], edx, and walking all 108 calls to it in the global initialiser at rvas 0x56E10..0x59320 pairs every id with the name literal it was constructed from - 0x2E = MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY (rva 0x57EB8), 0x2D = MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY (rva 0x57E63), 0x4B = MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA (rva 0x5886D), 0x0F = MODIFIER_IC (rva 0x573FD, where edx carries the 0xF set by lea edi,[ebx+0xF]) and 0x66 = MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (rva 0x59219). addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase_RoleByKey
addresses.comment: Start of the 33-way key chain in the sub-unit loader at rva 0x1AE1C0. Each step compares the definition's key against one hardcoded literal - the contiguous block 0x15C7750..0x15C794C, infantry_brigade through carrier - and on a match stores the definition pointer into one fixed slot of CSubUnitDataBase between +0x2C and +0xAC. The cached block is 33 slots, not 34: nothing in this function or anywhere else writes +0x28 through the database.
addresses.evidence: CSubUnitDataBase's loader is rva 0x1AE1C0, called once, from rva 0x237A7B, with the database, the parse node and a third value pushed on the stack. For every definition it parses it runs a chain of 33 inline string comparisons of the definition's key against one hardcoded literal each, and on a match stores the freshly built CSubUnitDefinition* into one fixed slot: rva 0x1AF867 pushes 'infantry_brigade' (0x15C7750) and rva 0x1AF8E7 stores to +0x34, and so on for all 33, ending at rva 0x1B01CE storing 'carrier' to +0xAC. The 33 literals sit contiguously in rdata from 0x15C7750 to 0x15C794C and each is referenced exactly once in the whole image, from this chain. addresses.name: CProvince_StorePort
addresses.comment: mov [ecx+0x354], eax - the only place a CProvince's CPort is set. ecx is the land province looked up out of the map's province array, eax a new 0x1C-byte CPort whose +0x18 holds the adjacent sea province id. Runs at map load, once per land-to-sea adjacency.
addresses.evidence: Written in exactly one place with a CProvince as the base: rva 0x90713, mov [ecx+0x354], eax, inside the function at rva 0x90390. ecx there is provinces[landTemplate->+0x7C] taken out of the map's province array at +0x2200, and eax is a freshly allocated 0x1C-byte object whose vftable is written as 0x15BE4A4 six instructions earlier at rva 0x90703. That address is CPort's virtual table in the RTTI class export and no other class's - vtable.py --holding 0x15BE4A4 reports it in none, and hoi3.classes() lists it only under CPort. The same block sets the new object's +0x18 to the sea template's +0x7C, the sea province id, and the branch is reached only after the neighbouring template's +0x22 sea flag tests non-zero, so one CPort is built per land-to-sea adjacency at map load. Its use as a gate is the pair at rvas 0x1CEEAD and 0xA7EF7, which read the template's sea flag, then an unidentified province field at +0x330, then province->+0x354 != 0, then province->+0x300->+0x20 > 0, and only then follow template->+0xA4 (the adjacent sea province id) into the sea. The only other store is rva 0x94AF8, the CProvince constructor clearing +0x340..+0x360 in one run, which is what makes null the meaningful 'no port' value. What would show it wrong: a second writer of +0x354 through a CProvince, or a CPort reached from elsewhere with different contents - a whole-image scan for the displacement 0x354 returned 104 sites and only these two have a province as the base.

struct_fields.name: port
struct_fields.comment: the province's map port - the link to the sea province beside it - or null where it has none. Built at map load from the land/sea adjacency, not from buildings.txt; the naval base building is the separate thing at +0x300, and the sea hop tests both.
struct_fields.evidence: Written in exactly one place with a CProvince as the base: rva 0x90713, mov [ecx+0x354], eax, inside the function at rva 0x90390. ecx there is provinces[landTemplate->+0x7C] taken out of the map's province array at +0x2200, and eax is a freshly allocated 0x1C-byte object whose vftable is written as 0x15BE4A4 six instructions earlier at rva 0x90703. That address is CPort's virtual table in the RTTI class export and no other class's - vtable.py --holding 0x15BE4A4 reports it in none, and hoi3.classes() lists it only under CPort. The same block sets the new object's +0x18 to the sea template's +0x7C, the sea province id, and the branch is reached only after the neighbouring template's +0x22 sea flag tests non-zero, so one CPort is built per land-to-sea adjacency at map load. Its use as a gate is the pair at rvas 0x1CEEAD and 0xA7EF7, which read the template's sea flag, then an unidentified province field at +0x330, then province->+0x354 != 0, then province->+0x300->+0x20 > 0, and only then follow template->+0xA4 (the adjacent sea province id) into the sea. The only other store is rva 0x94AF8, the CProvince constructor clearing +0x340..+0x360 in one run, which is what makes null the meaningful 'no port' value. What would show it wrong: a second writer of +0x354 through a CProvince, or a CPort reached from elsewhere with different contents - a whole-image scan for the displacement 0x354 returned 104 sites and only these two have a province as the base.
